chunks: My father and Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan, may Allāh have mercy on them both, narrated from Ḥasan ibn Mattīl, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Alī al-Kūfī, from ‘Alī ibn Ḥassān al-Hāshimī, from ‘Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Kathīr, the servant of Abī Ja‘far (peace be upon him), from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:

If one of you were to perform Ḥajj throughout his entire life, yet did not visit al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Alī (peace be upon him), he would have abandoned a right of Allāh and a right of the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family), because the right of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) is a mandatory obligation from Allāh, incumbent upon every Muslim.
ai.seo_question: Is visiting Imam Husain (a.s.) obligatory in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh presents this hadith to establish Ziyārah al-Ḥusayn not merely as a recommended act but as a compulsory obligation (farīḍah) equal in weight to Ḥajj. This elevates the visitation to the Imam of the Time from a devotional practice to a fundamental pillar of faith, ensuring that the spiritual legacy of the Ahl al-Bayt remains central to Islamic piety alongside the rituals of the pilgrimage.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 4. My father and Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan both narrated to me from Ḥasan ibn Mattīl, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali Al-Kūfi, from ‘Ali ibn Ḥassān Al-Hāshimi, from ‘Abdil Raḥmān ibn Kuthayr – the servant of Abī Ja’far (Imam Bāqir (a.s.)), who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:

Even if you go to Hajj every year of your life but do not go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.), you have abandoned one of your obligations toward Allāh and His Messenger (s.a.a.w.). Verily Allāh has made it mandatory (on the believers to fulfill) the right(s) of Ḥusain (a.s.), and this (Ziyārah) is obligatory on every Muslim.
